LFA (Light Flash Apparatus) - contactless measurement of thermal diffusivity, specific heat and thermal conductivity
Operating principle:
The LFA 467 HyperFlash is designed as a vertical system with the light source at the bottom to heat up the bottom side of a sample located at the middle position, and a detector on top to measure the temperature rise at the top side of the sample. A xenon lamp serves as the flash source. The variable pulse energy is software-controlled and an optional filter wheel can be used to further adjust it. The pulse width is adjustable in the range of 20 μs to 1200 μs. 
An advanced mercury cadmium telluride (MCT) detector is available and allows measurements from -100 °C to 500 °C. 
The instrumentation includes sophisticated hardware and simple menu-driven software to provide fast, accurate, and safe measurements. The LFA 467 works to the flash method according to international standards ASTM E 1461, ASTM E 2585, DIN EN 821-2, DIN 30905, ISO22007-4, ISO 18755, ISO 13826 BS EN 1159-2 and ASTM C-714* (* included in ASTM E1461).
Available sample holders:
25.4 x 25.4 mm standard square sample holder
Ø 25.4 mm standard round sample holder
Ø 12.7 mm thin foil sample holder
In-Plane Sample Holder (for measurements of a round sample in a horizontal direction) (for sample dimensions Ø 20 ... 25.4 mm, thickness 1 mm max)
In-Plane Sample Holder (for sample dimensions square or rectangular: 17 … 25.4 x 17 … 25.4 mm, thickness 1 mm max. or round: 23 ... 25.4 mm, thickness 1 mm max)
Applications and operation modes:
The LFA instrumentation can be used to measure the thermal diffusivity, specific heat and thermal conductivity of metals, graphite, coatings, composites, ceramics, polymers and other materials.​

Technical specifications
Netzsch LFA 467 HyperFlash
High temperature and high performance test instrument for contactless measurement of thermal diffusivity, specific heat and thermal conductivity in accordance to ASTM E 1461. 
Features:​​​​​​
Temperature Range: -100°C ... 500°C
Thermal diffusivity: 0.01 mm2/s ... 2000 mm2/s
Thermal conductivity: 0.1 W/(m·K) ... 4000 W/(m·K)
Atmosphere: Inert, oxidizing, static and dynamic
Location: room 01.08, Materials Engineering Building (MTM) 334-10
